clue.text: Issue period return

indicators.note: return asks for the word for period to be turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: A notice about a period of time being returned, as from a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TIME round to give EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something, such as a statement or a sound, is to send it out or emit it.

clue.text: Previous European member Edward granted immunity

parts.note: a previous partner or holder of a post is an ex
MP is a Member of Parliament
Ted is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A former Euro-MP called Edward has been given immunity from prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone granted immunity is excused, or freed, from an obligation or penalty.

clue.text: Compromise when business has finished

parts.note: trade is commerce, business in general
off can mean finished or over, as in a match called off

explanation.surface: A deal settled once the day's commerce has wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A balancing of one advantage against another is a compromise between competing aims.

clue.text: Sculptures that over the Channel are possessing formal dignity

parts.note: statues are sculptures of figures
que is French for that; France lies across the English Channel

explanation.surface: French sculptures are noted for their stately, dignified bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the Channel' means in French, from a British viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque describes someone tall, poised and dignified, like a statue in bearing.

clue.text: Bright star that's excellent, one appearing after 30 days

indicators.note: appearing after places the letter for one behind the month

parts.note: super is a colloquial word for excellent
November is a month of thirty days, abbreviated Nov
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A dazzling celebrity who turns up at the end of every month.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 days' points to a month of that length; NOV (November) fits, with A coming after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and briefly becomes extremely bright.

clue.text: Two angelic things offering slight hope of success

definitions.meaning: an angel is pictured with a wing and saying a prayer, two things linked with angels
the idiom for getting by on very little chance of success

explanation.surface: Two heavenly attributes give only a faint chance of things working out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for managing on luck alone describes a situation with only slight hope of success.

clue.text: Muse of terrible repute, fifth-rate

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word repute is mangled into a new order

parts.note: E is the fifth grade or letter, so fifth-rate gives E

explanation.surface: A goddess of the arts with a dreadful reputation, distinctly second-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges REPUTE into EUTERP, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over music and lyric poetry.

clue.text: Said choir meeting in wet low-lying ground

indicators.note: in places the meeting inside the sound-alike word
said shows the word choir is heard rather than spelt, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: choir is pronounced the same as quire, a set of sheets of paper
an AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A choir gathering in a soggy field.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a set of sheets of paper, which sounds just like choir; 'meeting' is the annual general meeting abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a bog, soft wet ground that gives way underfoot.

clue.text: See, say, inclusion of song of lamentation

indicators.note: inclusion of shows the example abbreviation is put inside the see

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city and see in England
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Look at, for instance, a mournful song included in the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb, but it is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or song, especially a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Scamper heartlessly round side of ditch

indicators.note: round suggests the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
heartlessly removes the central letter of the word scamper

explanation.surface: Run carelessly around the edge of a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the middle M of SCAMPER to leave SCAPER; 'round' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp, or escarpment, is the inner slope or wall of a defensive ditch.

clue.text: Start what I did in restaurant

definitions.meaning: to start something is to set it going
read as four words, describing eating inside an eatery

explanation.surface: Begin by describing a meal you had out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into IN IT I ATE: what I did in it, the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it or set it in motion.

clue.text: Exhibitionist rose up angrily

indicators.note: angrily suggests the letters of rose up are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A show-off got to their feet in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur affects an attitude to impress others, a kind of show-off.

clue.text: Spirited game?

parts.note: spirited read as made of spirits: two alcoholic drinks naming a card game

explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a card game whose name happens to combine two spirits.

clue.text: Too often changed comment at bottom of page

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of too often are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor's remark that the text gets amended too frequently.
explanation.definitionFit: A footnote is a note printed at the foot of a page.

clue.text: In an unhappy way complete a ripping job

explanation.surface: Weeping while finishing off a splendid piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as TEAR FULLY, tear rhyming with bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To act tearfully is to cry, which is behaving unhappily.

clue.text: Not able to hear fade away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters of fade wander off into a new order

explanation.surface: Sound fading so that it can no longer be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf means lacking the power of hearing.

clue.text: One in the capacity of breather for diving apparatus

parts.note: a means one
qua is Latin for in the capacity of
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: Someone acting as a breather for a diver.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqualung is breathing equipment worn by underwater divers.

clue.text: Witticism from Jack, Oriental holy man

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
E stands for eastern, oriental
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A joke told by an Eastern holy man called Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke or witty remark.

clue.text: Go in with Jim's sort of patriotism

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters are sorted, put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the name with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Join Jim in his flag-waving kind of national pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GOIN and JIMS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoism is extreme, aggressive patriotism.

clue.text: Genuine sportsman unswervingly faithful

definitions.meaning: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A real athlete who never wavers in loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an award at Oxford and Cambridge universities for representing them at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: True blue means staunchly loyal, steadfast in allegiance.

clue.text: Kelvin, American with Harry going back to endlessly dry desert

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, a unit of temperature

indicators.note: going back turns the short name round

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as with Prince Hal

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter of the word for dry

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: Kelvin and an American travel with Harry back to a parched, endless desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns HAL into LAH; 'endlessly' trims ARID to ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a large desert in southern Africa.

clue.text: Essential electronic noise having entered data

parts.note: key means essential, crucial
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Vital electronic noise accompanied the typing in of data.
explanation.definitionFit: To have keyed in data is to have typed it into a computer.

clue.text: Springtime in 2012?

parts.note: springtime read as a time for jumping, a year with an extra day such as that one

explanation.definitionFit: A year with 29 February, such as 2012, is a time named for a jump.

clue.text: In journal I believed it was defamation

indicators.note: In shows the letters sit inside the words journal I believed

explanation.surface: Someone thought a journal article was defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across journaL I BELieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is defamation in written or published form.

clue.text: Drawing of fruit by Yorkshire runner

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire; rivers run

explanation.surface: A sketch of fruit placed beside a Yorkshire athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river here: the Ure flows through Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a drawing or diagram, as in a numbered illustration.

clue.text: Jump a line to reach limit

parts.note: to bound is to jump
RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: Leap over a line to get as far as the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary is a dividing line marking a limit.

clue.text: I call a doctor who's not clerical

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so the letters of I call a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone summons a physician who is not one of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laical means of the laity, ordinary people rather than clergy.

clue.text: Lorry began transporting fruit

indicators.note: transporting suggests the letters of lorry began are carried off into a new order

explanation.surface: A truck started carrying a load of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A loganberry is a fruit, a hybrid of raspberry and blackberry.

clue.text: One can't go straight to centre of this complicated network

definitions.text: One can't go straight to centre of this complicated network

parts.words: One can't go straight to centre of this complicated network
parts.note: describes a puzzle of winding paths where the middle can only be reached by detours

explanation.definitionFit: A maze is a network of paths designed to confuse anyone trying to reach its centre.
